marks.gloss_en: is R' Eliezer then of the view that the read form governs (reading תרומתי as plural)? but in the baraita on בבגדו בה he reads the written form (בגד) -- unanswered; the 34a.3 account is abandoned at 34a.6
R' Akiva: 'bevigdo bah' -- once [the master] spread his garment over her, [the father] may no longer sell her
the baraita: 'a blemish' forbids inflicting one; whence that one may not put figs or dough on the ear for a dog to come and eat? 'any blemish' -- direct and indirect alike
Shmuel / Reish Lakish / Rabba bar Avuh: 'and I, behold, I have given you the charge of My terumot' (Num 18:8) -- the verse the teruma dispute turns on
(abandoned) R' Eliezer holds the verse speaks of two terumot, pure and in abeyance, and the Merciful One said: guard it
R' Eliezer: once [the father] dealt deceitfully with her, he may no longer sell her -- reading the written form
rather, the teruma tannaim dispute whether teruma in doubtful impurity counts as fit for you
Shmuel: the halakha follows R' Shimon (which R' Shimon is the question that follows; content left unspecified)
Rav: the halakha follows R' Yehuda [an unintended act is forbidden]
Shmuel's ruling follows the R' Shimon of the baraita (33b.7): the firstborn may even be slaughtered on account of the bloodletting blemish
R' Eliezer: one who slits the ear of a firstborn may never slaughter it
ומי קניס רבי אליעזר לעולם? ורמינהי: ... קצצה מתכוין, רבי אליעזר אומר: לכשיולד לו נגע אחר יטהר הימנו -- there he does not penalize forever
